nodes.description:
The only strategy here aimed at the lesion itself rather than at its consequences, and the one whose preclinical record most clearly identifies what would stop it working in a patient: getting the vector into the brain.
Several vectors have been tried in Ndufs4-null mice. AAV-PHP.B carrying human NDUFS4, delivered at postnatal day 26 to 28, extended lifespan and reduced disease severity across growth, motor coordination, failure to thrive, seizures and cardiac abnormalities. An AAV1 construct delivered bilaterally into the vestibular nuclei extended lifespan and delayed progression - which is also the observation that implicates those nuclei in the mouse's breathing failure.
The negative result is the informative one. Intravenous AAV2/9 carrying human NDUFS4 reached skeletal muscle, heart and liver, was absent from brain, and did not improve clinical symptoms. A disease whose lesions are in the brainstem is not treated by a vector that stops at the blood-brain barrier, and mouse and human barriers differ, so a delivery route that works in this animal does not transfer by default.

nodes.description:
NDUFS4 is one of about thirty accessory subunits of complex I, and its position is what makes it load-bearing. It sits at the interface between the N module, which oxidises NADH, and the Q module, which passes the electrons to ubiquinone, and it contacts subunits in both. The current reading of the experimental data is that NDUFS4 controls the attachment of the N module to the rest of the enzyme.
Losing it takes a second subunit with it. In both Ndufs4-null mouse cells and NDUFS4-mutant patient cells the accessory subunit NDUFA12 is almost entirely absent, while the assembly factor NDUFAF2 - which NDUFA12 would normally displace - accumulates. The relationship is one-way: NDUFA12-mutant patient cells do not lose NDUFS4.

nodes.description:
On a blue native gel, NDUFS4-mutant patient fibroblasts show no fully assembled complex I holoenzyme at all. What is present instead is a catalytically inactive subcomplex of about 830 kDa, carrying NDUFAF2 and lacking the N module. This profile is constant across every NDUFS4 allele that has been tested, which is unusual enough that it was proposed as a screening method: the gel plus the MRI identifies the gene.
One caveat belongs with the finding. In intact tissue, substantial rotenone-sensitive quinone-reductase activity survives, and Ndufs4-null mouse fibroblasts contain active complex I in situ - so the complete absence of holoenzyme on the gel partly reflects the complex falling apart during solubilisation. The enzyme in a living cell is destabilised, not necessarily wholly absent.

nodes.description:
The reported pathogenic alleles are frameshifts, nonsense variants and splice-altering variants, and what they have in common is more informative than what distinguishes them: almost all of them abolish full-length NDUFS4 protein. Where a truncated product would be predicted, the transcript itself is usually lost as well.
Founder alleles exist. A homozygous c.393dupA frameshift accounts for Leigh disease in the Hutterite population, where the carrier frequency was estimated at 1 in 27 across more than 1,300 individuals, and founder alleles have also been described in North Africa. A non-consanguineous family reached homozygosity by complete paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 5, which is worth knowing because a single-parent carrier test in that situation is falsely reassuring.

The enzymatic consequence, and it is isolated in the strict sense: the expression and activity of the other oxidative phosphorylation complexes are not affected. That is what puts this disease in the complex I deficiency nomenclature rather than in the combined respiratory-chain disorders, and it is measurable in the tissues that are biopsied - muscle in 18 of 22 reported patients, fibroblasts in 12.
In a patient fibroblast line, complex I activity is severely reduced and, distinctively, insensitive to cAMP stimulation - the NDUFS4 subunit carries the consensus site through which protein kinase A is thought to act on the complex.

nodes.description:
The most recent preclinical strategy and the one that follows from the emerging leukocyte-driven account of lesion formation. In Ndufs4 knockout mice a CSF1R inhibitor suppressed lesion formation, rescued seizures, respiratory function and hyperlactaemia and substantially extended survival.
It has not been tried in patients, and the step it targets has not been demonstrated in human NDUFS4 tissue - so this is a treatment aimed at a mechanism that is itself recorded here as emerging.

Proliferating leukocytes are not just present in the lesions; in the Ndufs4 knockout mouse they are causally required for them. Depleting leukocytes with a CSF1R inhibitor suppressed lesion formation, rescued seizures, respiratory centre function and hyperlactaemia, and substantially extended survival. The same work proposes this as the explanation for why mTOR inhibition works, which had been unexplained for nearly a decade.
Whether this is true of human NDUFS4 disease is untested. It is recorded because a causal immune step changes what a therapy would target, and because it is the strongest single mechanistic result to come out of this model since the rapamycin finding.

nodes.description:
CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of NDUFS4 in human induced pluripotent stem cells, with isogenic controls. Its value is the comparator: patient fibroblast lines differ from controls in their whole genetic background, whereas an isogenic knockout differs at one locus. The limitation the authors state themselves is that undifferentiated iPSCs cannot reproduce the cellular dynamics of the disease, so this is a redox and metabolic platform rather than a model of the encephalopathy.
`experimental_model_type` is OTHER rather than IPSC_DERIVED_MODEL on purpose. That value is defined as a *differentiated* model derived from induced pluripotent stem cells, and this one is deliberately undifferentiated, which is exactly what the authors' own caveat is about. CELL_LINE does not fit either, being defined for immortalized lines. OTHER is the accurate choice here rather than a placeholder.

Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes carrying an Ndufs4 deletion. This one is IPSC_DERIVED_MODEL rather than OTHER because the cells are differentiated into the affected cell type, which is the distinction the enum draws.
It is the human counterpart of the tissue-specific mouse work on the cardiac phenotype, and it does something the mouse cannot: it puts the cardiomyopathy in a human cardiomyocyte and traces it to a specific molecular step, a fall in NAD+/NADH leaving the cardiac sodium channel NaV1.5 hyperacetylated. The same paper reports NDUFS4-deleted iPSC-derived neurons.

Pyramidal signs in 6 of 22 patients (27%). The compilation records them as a category without itemising which signs, so the generic HPO term is bound rather than a specific one such as hyperreflexia or an extensor plantar response, neither of which the source names.

Downstream of the enzyme defect, patient-derived cells show partial mitochondrial membrane depolarisation, raised reactive oxygen species and raised NAD(P)H, disturbed cytosolic and mitochondrial calcium and ATP handling, and altered mitochondrial morphology. Pyruvate that cannot be oxidised is converted to lactate, which is what raises lactate in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid.
A CRISPR knockout of NDUFS4 in human induced pluripotent stem cells reproduces the redox half of this directly, with roughly half the complex I activity of isogenic controls and an elevated NADH/NAD+ ratio - useful because it is a human cell with a defined isogenic comparator rather than a patient line with an uncontrolled background.

nodes.description:
The reference model for this disease and one of the most heavily used models in mitochondrial medicine. It is unusually well matched to the human condition for a reason that is explicit in the literature: human NDUFS4 disease is autosomal recessive and its alleles abolish full-length protein in every cell, so a whole-body deletion reproduces the human genotype in kind rather than approximating it. The animal was made by deleting exon 2, producing a frameshift that prevents formation of NDUFS4 protein - the same lesion class as the human alleles.
Mice appear healthy for about five weeks, then develop ataxia, lethargy, blindness and raised lactate, and die at around seven weeks. The neuropathology is bilateral spongiform lesions in the vestibular nuclei with degeneration in the olfactory bulb, cerebellum and other structures.

The landmark preclinical result in this disease and still the most-replicated one. Untreated Ndufs4 knockout mice die at a median of 50 days; on daily rapamycin, median survival was 114 days in males and 111 in females, and the longest-lived animal reached 269. Treatment also delayed the onset of neurological signs, reduced neuroinflammation and prevented the brain lesions altogether in treated animals examined at 100 and 268 days.
It has not been tested in a controlled trial in NDUFS4 patients. The mechanism was unexplained for years and the leukocyte work now offers one - that rapamycin's benefit is largely immunosuppressive.
